rationale: Round 1 compiled and ran correctly with no ICE, so this candidate escalates obfuscation while respecting the profile: netbench-crc is a tiny (6 functions, ~1.4 KB text), table-driven benchmark whose hot paths are the crc32 table generation and per-packet CRC loops, so runtime-heavy transforms are raised only moderately (BCF RuntimeCost 0.55, FLA 0.5) to avoid unacceptable slowdown on those loops. Structural, low-risk passes are favored instead: SUB is weighted highest for security (arithmetic substitution directly obscures the CRC polynomial math and is nearly free), SPLIT and IGV get the highest DiversityGain since basic-block splitting and global-variable indirection add the most binary-level novelty to such a small, static layout, and ICALL/IBR obscure the very short call graph (6 functions) and control flow cheaply. CorrectnessRisk stays low across the board given round 1's clean result, but BCF/FLA/IGV retain modest risk weights because bogus predicates and loop flattening on the packet-processing state machine are the most likely sources of semantic drift in this codebase.
